memoryTip: Ubi-quity: the state of being everywhere.
correctPassage: The ubiquity of plastic waste is now visible even in remote polar waters.
wrongPassages: The style guide’s last “see ubiquity” joke was replaced with a real definition.
The trunk foam had an ubiquity-shaped hole and no matching tool.
The wallpaper-only ubiquity toggle was buried in accessibility settings.

memoryTip: In-noxious — not harmful; harmless remark.
correctPassage: What seemed an innocuous remark was later read as a coded insult.
wrongPassages: The innocuous solvent burned through steel and required full hazard suits.
Critics called the speech innocuous after it sparked unrest in three cities.
an innocuous password, in this guide, includes every personal detail an attacker wants.

definition: extremely complex and difficult to follow
memoryTip: Con-voluted: coiled like a volume of twists — overly complex.
correctPassage: The contract’s convoluted clauses obscured who actually held liability.
wrongPassages: The atrium’s convoluted light came from one skylight only at noon.
Admin tried to convoluted complaint volume by hiding the contact form.
His convoluted RFA set sought admissions about documents never exchanged.

memoryTip: Salient points “leap out” (salire = to leap) — most noticeable.
correctPassage: The most salient finding was the sharp drop in error rates after training.
wrongPassages: The icefall detour felt salient on a summer catwalk bolted to rock.
Her salient deposition notice omitted the remote link parties needed.
a salient approval test stores a screenshot of a blank page.

memoryTip: Throw a thwart across the boat — block the plan.
correctPassage: Bad weather threatened to thwart the launch for a third time.
wrongPassages: a thwart resume test never leaves the first checkpoint step.
Fans found the sequel’s opening thwart for answering the cliffhanger immediately.
The machine stayed thwart through a surge that reset every other device.

memoryTip: Im-pede (foot): put something in the path of the feet — slow progress.
correctPassage: Debris on the track will impede the train’s progress.
wrongPassages: an impede capacity plan is one optimistic row in a spreadsheet.
The subdominant drone was impede under a final V–I alone.
The held fifth was impede under a modulation that never returned to it.

memoryTip: Glean leftover grain from a field — pick up bits of info.
correctPassage: From scattered letters, historians can glean how the community responded.
wrongPassages: Quants discarded the glean factor that explained most of the variance.
The firm tried to bill glean time by rounding every six minutes upward.
The slip’s glean tide gauge needle was frozen mid-scale for months.

memoryTip: Ephemera last a day — short-lived.
correctPassage: Social media fame is often ephemeral, fading within weeks.
wrongPassages: Stone monuments are ephemeral because they outlast the generations that raise them.
Their ephemeral friendship has continued through thirty years of weekly letters.
He filed the ephemeral contract in a steel vault marked permanent archive.

memoryTip: In sporadic spots — now and then, irregularly.
correctPassage: The species appears only sporadically along the coast.
wrongPassages: They planned sporadically: the calendar blocked “TBD” for every afternoon next month.
The sensor sampled sporadically, capturing one point and declaring the series complete.
They audited sporadically, checking only the cover page of each folder.

memoryTip: Freighted with trouble — filled with risk or tension.
correctPassage: Negotiations were fraught with misunderstandings from the start.
wrongPassages: The org tried to fraught open tickets by auto-solving anything over thirty days old.
The motif sounded fraught after brass buried it completely.
The mole’s fraught foghorn schedule was for a season already over.

definition: in a way that suggests a good outcome
memoryTip: Auspicious = good omen (birds were once signs) — promising start.
correctPassage: The festival began auspiciously with clear skies and a full house.
wrongPassages: The choir sang auspiciously, holding one pitch for the entire piece.
She wrote auspiciously, filling the page with the same sentence copied ten times.
They voted auspiciously: every hand went up on the first call with no debate.

memoryTip: Hap + hazard — by chance, no plan, messy.
correctPassage: Files had been stored haphazardly, with no consistent naming system.
wrongPassages: They finished haphazardly by starting the work after the deadline had passed.
He packed haphazardly, putting breakable items at the bottom under the tools.
She answered haphazardly, which here meant she spoke for twenty minutes without a pause.

memoryTip: Antagonist in a story — opposing, hostile.
correctPassage: The two theories are not necessarily antagonistic; they address different scales.
wrongPassages: Her antagonistic report listed exact figures, dates, and sources for every claim.
Reviewers called the stats antagonistic after a reanalysis matched the paper.
The lay-by looked antagonistic at night with no lorries parked along it.

definition: the process of adding; a summary
memoryTip: Sum it up — summary or total.
correctPassage: The final chapter is a careful summation of the book’s main claims.
wrongPassages: Astronomers reserve summation for stars whose brightness never changes at all.
The packing card’s summation line was a doodle of a wrench.
He typed summation into the suffix field and the printer added it to the badge.

memoryTip: Un-equi-vocal: one voice only — crystal clear, no double meaning.
correctPassage: The data provide unequivocal support for the revised timeline.
wrongPassages: The ore dock looked unequivocal with loaders parked for a decade.
Her unequivocal attachment a was a blank PDF named “final-final.”
She ran an unequivocal errand list of one item already finished that morning.

memoryTip: Can’t reproach (blame) them — faultless conduct.
correctPassage: Her professional conduct throughout the inquiry was irreproachable.
wrongPassages: Critics called the clean version irreproachable for removing the song’s only edge.
The organ pedal was irreproachable once the manuals cadenced alone.
The submediant held was irreproachable under an ending that sat only on I.

memoryTip: Works by association — links of memory, not strict logic.
correctPassage: The poem relies on associative leaps rather than linear narrative.
wrongPassages: The cattle dock looked associative with ramps chained up for years.
The orchard looked associative after hail stripped every tree in a single hour.
The hallway was redesigned to be associative: a sealed cube with no doors.

definition: unable to be resisted or avoided
memoryTip: In-e-luctable: you can’t struggle free — unavoidable.
correctPassage: Climate models point to ineluctable warming under current emissions paths.
wrongPassages: He described the puzzle as ineluctable after solving it in under a minute.
Voters tabled the ineluctable transit tax that riders had already endorsed.
Reviewers called the staging ineluctable for ignoring the playwright’s pauses.

memoryTip: Ten-uous: thin as a tenuous thread — weak link.
correctPassage: The link between the two studies remains tenuous at best.
wrongPassages: The stand looked tenuous after packing when only chalk marks remained.
Fans found the hi-res reissue tenuous for files identical to the old CD master.
She closed the incident as tenuous with action items still ownerless.

definition: fail by trying to do too much
memoryTip: Reach too far — try too much and fail.
correctPassage: Critics accused the agency of regulatory overreach.
wrongPassages: The subtonic drone was overreach under a Picardy third that ignored it completely.
The salt flat stayed overreach under a model with a permanent drought.
The reservoir stayed overreach under a rule that banned any drawdown.
